question: How much compensation do I get under EU261 if my 1,500 km flight arrives 3 hours late?
rule: Passengers whose flight of 1,500 kilometres or less arrives three hours or more late are entitled to compensation of EUR 250 under Article 7 of Regulation (EC) No 261/2004.

question: When does an airline not have to pay EU261 compensation?
rule: An operating air carrier is not obliged to pay compensation under Article 5(3) of Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 if the cancellation is caused by extraordinary circumstances which could not have been avoided even if all reasonable measures had been taken.

question: How long do I have to return something I bought online in the EU?
rule: Under Article 9 of Directive 2011/83/EU on consumer rights, a consumer has a period of 14 days to withdraw from a distance contract without giving any reason.

question: How long is the legal guarantee on goods in the EU?
rule: Under Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2019/771, the seller is liable for any lack of conformity which exists at the time of delivery and becomes apparent within two years of that time.

question: How fast must a company answer my GDPR data access request?
rule: Under Article 12(3) of the GDPR, the controller must provide information on action taken on an access request without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request.

question: How much compensation do I get in the EU if my train is an hour late?
rule: Under Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passengers' rights, passengers are entitled to compensation of 25 % of the ticket price for a delay of 60 to 119 minutes.

question: What are my rights in the EU if my long-distance bus is delayed by two hours?
rule: Under Article 19 of Regulation (EU) No 181/2011, where a regular bus or coach service is delayed in departure for more than 120 minutes, passengers shall be offered continuation, re-routing or reimbursement of the ticket price.

question: What is the maximum payment term between businesses in the EU?
rule: Under Directive 2011/7/EU on combating late payment, payment periods in commercial transactions between undertakings should not exceed 60 calendar days unless expressly agreed and not grossly unfair to the creditor.

question: How long do I have to reject faulty goods in the UK?
rule: Under section 22 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015, the time limit for exercising the short-term right to reject faulty goods is 30 days.

question: How long does my landlord in England have to protect my deposit?
rule: Under section 213 of the Housing Act 2004, a landlord in England must protect a tenant's deposit in an authorised scheme and give the prescribed information within 30 days of receiving it.
